Kylian Mbappe's comments on Mao Zedong have drawn the ire of the Chinese [Violeta Santos Moura/Reuters]By Manasi Pathak, AFP and ReutersPublished On 28 Oct 202628 Oct 2026
Real Madrid’s Kylian Mbappe is at the centre of a controversy in China for his comments on late Chinese leader Mao Zedong, which have not only cost him several commercial deals but have also led to state television scrapping La Liga broadcasts.
The backlash highlighted the risks for athletes and brands ⁠in the lucrative Chinese market, where satire about Mao, modern China’s founding leader who ruled the country from 1949 until his death in 1976, remains a social taboo.

Once hailed as a footballing sensation, Mbappe was widely adored in China until the controversy caused outrage among the country’s 1.4 billion people.
Despite issuing an apology, the French superstar struggled to dissipate anger on Chinese social media on Wednesday.
Al Jazeera breaks down the row between Mbappe and China:
What did Mbappe say about Mao?
A video circulated online showed France’s 2018 World Cup winner Mbappe apparently joking about a former Chinese leader.
While Mbappe did not name Mao in the video, he appeared to say the funniest internet meme he had seen was of his face digitally altered onto that of “some guy – I think he’s a Chinese dictator”.

Gulf countries have stepped up diplomacy with Iran in a bid to de-escalate tensions across the Middle East, amid fears of renewed US strikes on Tehran and intensifying hostilities between Iran-backed Houthi rebels in Yemen and Saudi Arabia.
The three nations that signed the Mecca Joint Defence Agreement in August – Pakistan, Saudi Arabia and Turkiye – and diplomats from Qatar met with high-ranking Iranian officials on Monday in an effort to prevent the resumption of all-out war.

Shadman Islam has scored two previous centuries in Test cricket [AFP]By AFPPublished On 28 Oct 202628 Oct 2026
Opener Shadman Islam hit an unbeaten 99 to steer Bangladesh to 213-3 on the opening day of the first cricket Test against the West Indies.
The left-hander was on the verge of his third Test century when bad light ended play after 74 overs at the start of the two-match series in Mirpur, Bangladesh.
Recommended Stories list of 4 itemslist 1 of 4Club in crisis: What are Manchester United’s top five problems?list 2 of 4Five major upsets in English football before Arsenal’s League Cup shocklist 3 of 4Carrick stays on as Manchester United manager for crucial Chelsea matchlist 4 of 4Can Carrick survive Man United’s slump and Fernandes fallout?end of list
Shadman hit 10 fours in his 219-ball stay, with Litton Das on 10 not out.
“It was nerve-racking even for us — at the end of the day, the whole team was nervous because everyone wanted him to get to his hundred,” Bangladesh batting coach Mohammad Salahuddin said on Wednesday.
“He has played around 30 (32) Test matches but has only two centuries, and I think that number should have been higher.”
Towhid Hridoy retired hurt on 42 due to cramps after he and Shadman added 88 runs for the fourth wicket to steady the Bangladesh innings.
West Indies struck early when in-form opener Tanzid Hasan edged Jayden Seales to second slip for nine.
Mominul Haque added 28 before falling to Jomel Warrican’s left-arm spin.
Shadman guided Bangladesh to lunch at 96-2, before Warrican struck again shortly after the break to trap Bangladesh captain Najmul Hossain Shanto leg before wicket for 19.

Brazilian Senator Flavio Bolsonaro disembarks from a plane after arriving at Opa-locka Executive Airport near Miami, Florida, US, October 28, 2026 [Eva Marie Uzcategui/Reuters]By AP and ReutersPublished On 28 Oct 202628 Oct 2026
Brazilian Senator Flavio Bolsonaro and his family have landed in Miami, Florida, after the candidate lost Sunday’s presidential election to incumbent Luiz Inacio Lula da Silva.
Bolsonaro and his family have been granted entry visas by the United States government after he refused to comply with a Brazilian Supreme Court order to surrender his passports.
The order was related to a money-laundering investigation in which he denies wrongdoing.
The Bolsonaro family’s journey to the US has drawn attention across the region.
Bolsonaro first fled from Brazil to Argentina and then to Ecuador alongside his wife and two daughters, Argentina’s migration authority said Wednesday.
According to Argentina’s migration department, they entered northern Argentina late on Tuesday before boarding a private jet to Guayaquil, Ecuador, and continuing to Miami.
This is a developing story.

While two wars on Iran by the United States and Israel have exposed serious vulnerabilities in Iran’s intelligence and security institutions, Iran is using the threat to crack down on dissent, analysts have said.
Saeid Golkar, an associate professor in political science at the University of Tennessee at Chattanooga, said the genuine espionage threats faced by Iran were illustrated by the killing of high-level figures, including former Supreme Leader Ayatollah Ali Khamenei, on the first day of the latest assault by Israel and the US on February 28.

“At the same time, the regime has historically used real or, most of the time, perceived security threats to justify political repression and expand its coercive apparatus,” Golkar told Al Jazeera.
“The current crackdown appears to reflect both legitimate counterintelligence concerns and the regime’s broader efforts to suppress dissent and intimidate society.”
Spy threat
Former Israeli spy chief David Barnea recently said that in the weeks before Israel launched its 12-day war on Iran in June 2025, he had approved the entry into the country of dozens of agents with clear intelligence or sabotage assignments.
“I can’t say that they are here with us. But they are there in Tehran, living their lives,” he told a conference in Israel on October 22.
